_doc: Which citations the manifesto's own repair worklists condemn, and which they merely mention. Read by tools/citation_gate.py, which refuses to let a condemned one appear in a published Codex lesson. Classify by NAME + YEAR: the year is usually what makes a citation false, and the same author often has a real work too.
_why_this_file_is_hand_curated: The worklists name the offender and its replacement in the same sentence — 'phantom futurist Elaine Day (2015) ... Weak-signal analysis belongs to Ansoff/Hiltunen' — so no regex can tell which of the two is the problem. A machine-derived list would condemn the fix.

The ratchet in the gate covers the cost of curating by hand: every Author (YYYY) the worklists mention must appear below as flagged or cleared, or the gate fails. A newly condemned source cannot be silently missed, which is the failure mode of every hand-maintained list.

cleared.name: Rogers
cleared.why: Carl Rogers, On Becoming a Person (1961) — real, and cited correctly in ch3/ch4/ch7. The worklist's objection is the ch8-s2 SHUFFLE, where a Granovetter weak-ties quote was matched to it. Same surname as the flagged Rogers (2022), different person, different verdict — which is the whole reason this gate matches on name AND year

cleared.why: Frey & Osborne are real. The Vol 2 worklist marks the ch45-s4 pair STILL OPEN as a STUDYBY-HIGH pattern rather than condemning it, so this gate does not condemn it either. The year remains unverified and belongs to the ORG-VERB/STUDYBY residual work

cleared.name: Osborne

cleared.name: Google
cleared.why: CORRECTED 2026-09-08. The worklist condemns a CONSTRUCTION -- the person-as-subject 'Google and Qualcomm (2023) found...' -- not the name. Every live instance is a legitimate organizational author, '(Google, 2023)' sitting beside '(Apple, 2023)' and '(Microsoft, 2023)' for the differential-privacy library and Google Translate. Flagging the bare name+year condemned 14 correct citations, which is precisely the cry-wolf failure this gate exists to avoid

cleared.name: Tech
cleared.why: same correction as Google (2023): 'Tech and Harvard (2023)' is a mangled construction already treated by fix_person_subject.py, not a condemned source

cleared.name: Bits
cleared.why: same correction: 'MIT Center for Bits and Atoms (2023)' is a real organizational author; only the person-as-subject phrasing was the defect, and it survives solely in an _audit-staging backup the source scan excludes

cleared.name: Seto
cleared.why: RECLASSIFIED 2026-09-08, after the fabrication it collided with was repaired. The condemned Seto (2016) was 'Michael Seto', a phantom Kardashev paper in a Journal of Big History volume that did not exist that year; ch4-s6 no longer cites it. What remains under this name+year is Karen C. Seto's real 'Carbon lock-in: Types, causes, and policy implications', Annual Review of Environment and Resources 41, 425-452, cited correctly in ch21 and ch38. Same surname, same year, different scholar -- repairing the fabrication is what makes this safe to clear

cleared.name: Rogers
cleared.why: RECLASSIFIED 2026-09-08. Nine instances were Everett Rogers (d. 2004) re-dated from Diffusion of Innovations (2003), Roo Rogers of Botsman & Rogers (2010), and Carl Rogers (1961) on person-centred design -- all repaired against each file's OWN reference list, which already carried the correct year. What remains is John A. Rogers, the materials scientist, in a ch27 energy-autonomous-sensing reference no worklist condemns. NOT a statement that that paper is real: it is unverified, and flagged for a human in the session report. It is simply not this gate's finding

cleared.name: Piketty
cleared.why: RECLASSIFIED 2026-09-08. The re-dated Capital citations went to 2014 (Belknap, Goldhammer as translator, not co-author) and one fabricated title, 'Capital concentration spiral', was deleted as an orphan. What remains is Chancel, Piketty, Saez & Zucman's World Inequality Report 2022, Harvard University Press -- genuinely 2022, verified

source._doc: The manifesto corpus itself. The lesson scan answers 'did a fabrication reach the public'; this answers 'is it still in the book'. Denylist, not allowlist: an allowlist of volumes silently misses the next volume, while a new ops doc merely shows up as findings. The worklists are excluded because cataloguing a condemned citation is their job.
